metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Cherry Valley, PA | Butler County
metaDescription: Cherry Valley sits in Butler County oil-and-gas country that predates Marcellus by a century. We buy legacy and modern mineral interests from PA owners directly, no broker.
heroLead: Butler County was drilling shallow oil and gas wells before most of Pennsylvania had electricity, and Cherry Valley families often own two very different kinds of mineral interest without realizing it.
intro: Our family sold our own minerals years ago, so we know what it's like to sit at the kitchen table with a stack of old paperwork trying to figure out what you actually own. Cherry Valley is a smaller community in Butler County, and what we see most often here isn't a single clean deed, it's a patchwork: a shallow gas lease from decades back that's still technically active, layered under whatever Marcellus-depth rights exist below it.

Those two intervals, shallow and deep, are often owned and leased separately in this part of the county. If you've got an old royalty check from a well nobody's thought about in years, or you've been contacted about a newer Marcellus unit, we can look at both and make you a cash offer on whichever piece, or both, makes sense to sell.

sections.heading: Two Layers of Gas History in One County
paragraphs: Butler County's shallow gas fields go back to the early 1900s, with thousands of legacy wells drilled into formations well above the Marcellus. Many of those old leases used simple one-eighth royalty language and never anticipated horizontal drilling into deeper shale. When Marcellus development reached this part of the county, some owners found their shallow rights and deep rights had been split apart entirely, sometimes without them ever being told.
If you're not sure whether your Cherry Valley interest is shallow, deep, or both, that's exactly the kind of thing we sort out before ever putting a number in front of you.

sections.heading: Small Working Interests and Stripper Wells
paragraphs: Because of that shallow-well history, some Cherry Valley families ended up with small non-operated working interests, not only royalty, from old wells drilled on their land generations ago. Those interests can come with joint interest billing statements, plugging liability questions, and other headaches a straight royalty owner never deals with. We evaluate those differently than a clean royalty interest, but we do buy them.
If your mail includes anything that looks like an operating statement rather than just a royalty check, hang onto it. It tells us something important about what you actually hold.

sections.heading: What the Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act Changed
paragraphs: Pennsylvania's Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act requires leases to guarantee at least a one-eighth royalty before deductions, but it doesn't ban post-production cost deductions the way some owners assume. A lot of the frustration we hear from Butler County families comes from that gap between what the law guarantees and what actually lands on the check after gathering and compression fees. We'll tell you plainly whether your deductions look ordinary for this area or not.

faqs.question: Do I own shallow rights, Marcellus rights, or both near Cherry Valley?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on how your deed and any prior leases were written. Butler County has a long shallow-gas history layered under newer Marcellus development, and the two are often held separately.

faqs.question: I have an old working interest in a small well, not only a royalty. Do you buy that?
faqs.answer: We evaluate working interests differently than royalty interests, but yes, we do consider them, including small legacy stripper-well interests.

faqs.question: Why did my royalty check drop even though the well is still producing?
faqs.answer: Usually post-production cost deductions, natural decline in the well's output, or both. Send us your statement and we'll walk through it honestly.
